Why does glass shatter so fast?

Every medium made of atoms has a speed of sound, which is essentially how fast a disturbance can move through that substance. There are several factors that determine this speed of interaction, but it tends to be faster in denser objects, because particles have less room to move around before bumping into a neighbor.

When you break a piece of glass, the cracks propagate through the piece at around the speed of sound in glass, which is much higher than the speed of sound in air. When a fracture forms, it ripples throughout the substance and tears it apart along lines where the bonds are weakest.
